item.title: Widening the lens: genetic testing barriers risk compounding prostate cancer inequalities
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor, I am very grateful to Naqvi and colleagues for highlighting the urgent need to address ethnic inequalities in prostate cancer outcomes. If the NSC does go ahead with a recommendation to introduce targeted screening for men aged 45 to 61 with BRCA1 and BRCA2 gene mutations, I fear that this will not only fail Black men but will also create new barriers for a much broader group of men (2). item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor, We read with interest this article, which raises important and very pertinent issues. item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor, Ebikeme’s feature captures a tension that is familiar in primary care: the same product can plausibly reduce harm for one group while creating new harms for another, and legislation must work in the messy middle where smoking, dual use, relapse, and social inequality coexist (1). item.title: Misleading editorial about evaluating new screening tests for breast cancer
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor The authors write that early detection of breast cancer “reduces mortality” (1). This is not correct. An apparent effect on breast cancer mortality in the mammography screening trials cannot be translated into an effect on mortality because breast cancer mortality is a flawed outcome. item.title: Re: Medicine is difficult—there are no shortcuts
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor Prof Elder's Opinion article attempts to highlight all the reasons why medical practice always has and always will remain hard.
